outlaws.name: Orrin Vask

token.name: Vask's Counting Bead
token.description: A counting bead darkened by handling. Vask used it to keep his place when the lots changed hands.

successor.name: Delia Vask
successor.story: Orrin's partner in the slave trade from the start, and the one who did the bargaining. She kept the buyers and the routes and changed nothing else.

outlaws.about: A slaver who buys cheap on the border and sells dear in the Nation's farms. He keeps his ledgers neater than his pens.

outlaws.name: Aldric Roane

token.name: Roane's Cut Seal
token.description: A seal cut from a piece of Holy Nation kit. Roane wore the blank reverse outwards.

successor.name: Brother Hale
successor.relation: the man who ran with him
successor.story: Deserted the Holy Nation the same night as Roane and has covered his back ever since. He still leads that frightened band through the Nation's hills.

outlaws.about: Once a Holy Sentinel, now wanted by the people he used to march with. He left the Nation over something he won't talk about.

outlaws.name: Karrash Red-Hand

token.name: Red-Hand's Ochre Tooth
token.description: A tooth coloured with red ochre. Fresh pigment sits in the grain beneath the worn face.

successor.name: Karrash the Younger
successor.story: Karrash Red-Hand's son, raised among berserkers and painted red before he could walk. He took his father's place at the next fight.

outlaws.about: A berserker who paints his hands in the blood of his last fight and doesn't wash until the next one.

outlaws.name: Veth of the Closed Hand

token.name: Veth's Spoils Counter
token.description: A flat counter polished on one side. Veth put it down before deciding what each fighter received.

successor.name: Veth of the Open Hand
successor.relation: the drone that broke with him
successor.story: A drone that broke with Veth over how to share the spoils, then came back to take the band once Veth was gone. It shares more, and the band likes it better.

outlaws.about: A hiveless drone who runs a band of outcasts in the north. It trades fairly and fights unfairly.

outlaws.name: Hollis Gantry

token.name: Gantry's Salvage Tag
token.description: A salvage tag bent around an old screw. The original machine number is still legible.

successor.name: Tam Gantry
successor.story: Hollis's nephew, sent to learn the scavenging trade and good at it from the start. He sells the old world's junk to anyone who pays.

outlaws.about: A tech hunter who stopped asking permission to dig in other people's ruins. The towns he sells to don't ask either.

outlaws.name: Gaffer Marrowbone

token.name: Marrowbone's Split Knuckle
token.description: A knuckle chipped open along the joint. The cord runs through a hole widened by long wear.

successor.name: Old Gristlejaw
successor.story: The eldest of Marrowbone's hunters, who has outlived three chiefs already. The cannibals follow him because he always finds meat.

outlaws.about: An old cannibal chief, scarred and slow, who has outlived every hunter sent after him.

outlaws.name: Rennik Salt

token.name: Rennik's Salt-Stiff Cord
token.description: A cord with salt caught between the strands. Rennik cut the knots to mark the road camps.

successor.name: Brin Salt
successor.story: Rennik's daughter, born in a dust camp and raised on the road. She keeps her father's camps moving along the roads.

outlaws.about: A dust boss who camps by the trade roads and takes a cut of whatever passes. He calls it rent.

outlaws.name: Slate Fennick

token.name: Fennick's Spare Strap Plate
token.description: A strap plate punched by hand. Fennick kept it for the next harness that tore on the road.

successor.name: Corra Fennick
successor.story: Slate's sister, who ran the band's camps and supplies. She picked up his sword and found the men already used to taking her orders.

outlaws.about: An outlaw swordsman who sells his blade to whoever pays first, and has been on both sides of most feuds in the border country.

outlaws.name: Brannoch Teel

token.name: Teel's Trail Peg
token.description: A hardwood peg sharpened again and again. Teel stuck it beside the tracks when a trail split.

successor.name: Wade Teel
successor.story: Brannoch's brother and the better tracker of the two. Runaways who thought the hunt was over learned otherwise.

outlaws.about: A slave hunter who brings runaways back for the reward and doesn't much care whose they were.

outlaws.name: Hob Lenner

token.name: Lenner's Water Gauge
token.description: A marker scored with three water levels. Lenner blackened the highest line with a coal.

successor.name: Ness Lenner
successor.story: Hob's first mate, who knew the coast and the tides better than he ever did. The crew voted for her before his body was cold.

outlaws.about: A reaver who raids the coast from small boats and is gone before the alarm bell stops ringing.

outlaws.name: Dolan Pike

token.name: Pike's Patched Spoon
token.description: A spoon pinned together at the neck. Pike had worn it down to the metal on both sides.

successor.name: Scrag Pike
successor.story: Dolan's cousin, as hungry and as desperate as the rest of the band. He leads by finding food first and sharing it second.

outlaws.about: Leader of a starving band that grew too big to feed. They take what they need from anyone on the road.

outlaws.name: Isolde Marr

token.name: Marr's Muster Clip
token.description: A clip from the company's muster roll. One corner is still caught under a bent tab.

successor.name: Bram Ostler
successor.story: Isolde's sergeant for eight years, who kept the company in line while she found the work. Now he finds the work as well.

outlaws.about: A mercenary captain whose company works for anyone with the cats, outlaws included. She's turned down more jobs than she's taken, but never for being too dirty.

say: Anti-Slavers keep a list of names, and one name keeps coming back. Orrin Vask runs the floodwaters. A woman with a scarf has been asking about him. Is she yours?
Orrin Vask is a name we hate. He trades in runaways. Someone in your company has been asking where he sleeps. Talk to the Swamp first.
You're travelling with someone who wants Vask. So do we. Ask a Swamper who has seen his boats.
Vask owns the river road and nobody talks about it. Whoever you travel with has reasons. Ask the Swamp, then end him.
accepted: Ask a Swamper in the town. They know his boats. Then end Vask and come to me.
A Swamper first. Then Vask. The Anti-Slavers pay on proof.
Start in the Swamp. Someone saw his boats and will tell you if you say who sent you.
Find a Swamper. They remember the night the river ran red. Then finish it.

say: Vask? Anti-Slavers sent you. His boats come through at night, low in the water. Two lamps. Kill him on the road, not in a town.
That name. Keep it down. Vask works the floodwastes and the mud between. He moves on, never twice the same week.
I saw Vask once. A fat smile and a long boat. If you can end him, you'll save more than you know.
He has taken ten of ours this year. I'll tell you where he was last. After that, you're on your own.
after: Out on the desert side of the floodwaters. Take plenty of water. And do not stand near a lamp.
Mud and desert both. Look for the long boats. You will know them.
South and east of the mud. He does not stay still. Neither should you.
Whatever you do, do not trust a smile out there.

say: Vask is dead? Then somebody's wife sleeps tonight. The Anti-Slavers thank you. Here are the cats.
The river road is quiet. Good work. The Anti-Slavers pay what they promised.
You ended him. I won't ask how.
A name off the list. That's worth more than coin, but here's coin too.
A former sergeant in your squad has been asking about Aldric Roane. That name is poison here. Roane sold a gate and left a man holding the blame.
The Hub remembers those who lie. Roane lies better than any. Someone with you wants his head, and so do I.
Aldric Roane. Don't say it loud. He has friends in the holy lands. A man travelling with you was his sergeant.
You aren't the first to ask. Roane has a purse and a band, and a poor sleeper's conscience. Bring him down.
accepted: Ask the Traders Guild who bought Roane's stolen gate. The wagon men know. Then finish him.
A trader first. Roane spent his coin where somebody will remember. Then Roane.
The Guild keeps ledgers. Ask a Guild man about a holy purse. Then go.
Find a Guild man and say Roane. Then find Roane. Report back.

say: Roane? I remember the purse. A holy captain bought a cart and two swords, then rode north of the Gulf. He was nervous.
A holy captain spent stolen coin here. Cart, swords, a fine hat. He paid in the Flame's own marks. Heading for the Pride.
The Guild doesn't ask. We write it down. A man called Roane bought arms and rode toward the Pride with a hired band.
Ah, a holy officer who paid in the wrong coin. North of the Gulf, near the pilgrim road. That's all the ledger says.
after: The pilgrim road, past the farms. Watch for outlaws in holy cloth.
Between the fields and the forest. I would not go alone.
He rode with outlaws wearing a soldier's cloth. They will not hide it.
No. But a man like that wants to be near the Flame he left. Look there.

say: Roane is dead. Then the Flame is a little cleaner. Here's coin from an honest man.
A traitor ended. I would pray for him, but not tonight. Take this.
You did what the Nation wouldn't.
Aldric Roane. The Hub drinks to you.
A Shek with you has been asking after Karrash Red-Hand. We know the name. He took a southern post and left no one to bury. Find him, flatskin.
Red-Hand is a name the Kingdom doesn't say twice. Someone travelling with you has reason to want his skull.
The Berserker called Red-Hand rides the mountains. A warrior with you was at the post he took. The Kingdom has no more to say.
A warrior carries a grudge until it kills her. Karrash Red-Hand has taken our people. End him and we'll pay.
accepted: Ask the shopkeepers in our towns. They hear what riders say. Then find the Berserker and finish it.
A Shek merchant first. They trade with everyone. Then Red-Hand.
Speak to a shopkeeper in any Shek town. Then go to the mountains and end him.
First the merchants. They know the Berserker's roads. Then you know what to do.

say: Red-Hand? A rider stopped here last week, speaking of him. He raids the canyonlands and hides in the mountain passes.
You ask about Karrash Red-Hand. I sell water to those who pass. Berserkers pass.
That name sells poorly. But yes. He raids from the desert mountains and leaves nobody. I will tell you where.
I sell goods. I hear things. Red-Hand rides in the mountain passes, between our posts.
after: Between the canyons and the desert. A Shek warrior would find him. A flatskin may die trying.
He uses the passes. Do not follow him in. Make him come out.
He will be at his camp. Berserkers do not hide. They wait.
Not long ago. He moves with a small band. Strong. Do not underestimate them.

say: Red-Hand is dead. The Kingdom is a little safer. Take the cats, flatskin.
A Berserker fewer. The warriors will drink to you.
You ended him. A flatskin did what a Shek couldn't.
A name struck from the rolls. The Kingdom pays its debts.
A quiet one among your company has been asking about Veth of the Closed Hand. We've heard of him. He leads those who were sent out, and they follow him.
Veth of the Closed Hand. We know the name. He took a Prince's command and left him to wander. We are told the exile is with you.
Someone travelling with you carries a grief for Veth. We feel it from here. We would like it ended.
You carry a Prince who was cast out. Veth is the one who did it. We can't say more. We hope you can do what we can't.
accepted: Speak to the Tech Hunters. They watch the Dark Fingers. They will know where Veth makes his camp.
A Tech Hunter first. They see all the roads. Then Veth.
Find a Tech Hunter. Ask about the Closed Hand. Then go.
Tech Hunters trade near the Fingers. They have seen him. Then finish it, if you must.

say: Veth? Hive outcast with a band. They camp near the Dark Fingers and chase anyone who looks too long. Not worth your trouble, honestly.
The one with the closed fist. I sold him bandages once. He pays in strange coin. His camp is near the old stones.
A Hive Prince with followers. The stones hum around his camp.
Tell me why I would help you find him? Cats? Fine. He sleeps near the Fingers, in the lee of the ridge.
after: The north side, in the lee. Do not come at dawn. They wake easily.
Nothing, I think. He wants to be left alone. That is the problem.
Careful. A Prince is clever, even outcast. Do not underestimate him.
East of the stones. You will smell him before you see him.

report.state: Veth of the Closed Hand killed by player
say: Veth is gone? The hive won't mourn. Take the cats. We hope the quiet one sleeps better.
A Prince fewer. The wastes are gentler.
You ended him. The hive doesn't say thank you, but we do.
He was a lonely one. Now he isn't.
Observation. A tinkerer in your company is looking for Hollis Gantry. He's a Tech Hunter who sells our dead for parts. We would like him disabled.
Hollis Gantry sells Skeleton chassis by the piece. A tinkerer travelling with you has a friend among the pieces. We'll pay for his removal.
The name Hollis Gantry is on our list. Someone with you has reason. We have reason too.
A tinkerer inquired about Gantry. We decline to explain. We'll pay for his deactivation.
accepted: Ask the Tech Hunters about their ruin crews. Gantry once worked for them. Then find him in the Graveyard.
A Tech Hunter first. They keep records. Then Gantry.
Tech Hunters dislike him. They may talk. Then deactivate him.
Find a Tech Hunter who knows his routes. Then proceed.

say: Gantry? He worked a ruin crew for us. Left with a crate of Skeleton parts and no explanation. We don't claim him.
Hollis Gantry stripped three Skeletons last month. We cut him loose. He works the Robot Graveyard with a small crew.
That name. I won't say much. He sold bad parts and ruined a ruin. He's near the graveyard.
Gantry? We aren't proud of him. He robs graves. Robot ones. He uses the old ruins as cover.
after: Near the Robot Graveyard. Keep your lantern off. His crew sleeps lightly.
Three, four. All armed. Do not rush.
Be careful. He knows the graveyard better than you.
Skeleton parts. Mostly limbs. Do not buy from him.

say: Gantry is disabled. The Skeletons note your service.
A grave-robber fewer. We approve. Cats follow.
Deactivated. Efficient. Here's your reward.
The tinkerer will rest easier. Here's the payment.
Gaffer Marrowbone is a name the Hunters spit. He took a hunting party at dinner. A survivor travels with you, I'm told. We pay for his end.
Marrowbone. We have a ledger of his meals. One of the names is Hale. A former hunter is with you, I hear. Finish this.
The Gaffer has fed on too many of ours. A man with you wants him. We want him.
Marrowbone is old and sly. A hunter with you knows the plains. Take him, and take Marrowbone.
accepted: Ask the Deadcat fishermen. They hear the cannibals' stories from the water. Then go to the badlands.
A fisherman first. They see the raiders' boats and fires. Then Marrowbone.
Find a Deadcat man. Ask about the Gaffer. Then finish it.
Deadcat talk goes both ways. Ask them. Then the badlands.

say: The Gaffer? He raids the coast in spring. Old man, big spoon, bigger appetite. He camps in the badlands.
Marrowbone. I've seen his fires. Hungry hunters on the dunes. He's out past the bone-fields.
An old cannibal who talks to the dead. We keep away from him. He's in the badlands, east of here.
That name. Don't say it near the fires. He was in the dunes last week, with a small crowd.
after: A dozen, on a good day. All hungry. Bring a fire and burn the camp.
East of the bone-fields. You will smell it before you see it.
Careful. He talks. Do not listen. He talks you into the pot.
Fire and salt. Nothing else works, I am told.

say: Marrowbone is dead? Then the plains are a little safer. The Hunters pay.
A cannibal fewer, and an old one. We thank you.
You ended the Gaffer. Hale will sleep better.
The Hunters drink to you. Take the coin.
The Guild keeps its records. A caravan of ours didn't arrive on the dust road. A Scorchlander with you may know the details. Rennik Salt took it, and we want him.
Rennik Salt owes the Guild eight carts and twelve lives. A surviving guard travels with you, I hear. Finish him.
The Guild is patient. Salt was a bandit with a good ledger. Someone with you has the other half of it.
Rennik Salt took a Guild caravan. Someone with you saw it. We pay for the man and the cargo.
accepted: Ask a United Cities guard about the dust road. They keep a map of raids. Then find Salt in the hills.
A guard first. They know his camps. Then Salt.
Find a City guard and ask about Dust Bandits. Then do what must be done.
A UC watchman will have his locations. Then the hills.

say: Rennik Salt? Dust Bandit boss. He hits caravans near the ancient hills and sells the cargo in the dust towns.
Salt. The name makes people quiet. He takes the high ground and doesn't let a cart pass. He's near the hills.
A bandit with a ledger. His camp moves with the weather. Last seen near the dry edge.
We have a file on Salt. He's cunning. He uses the hills as a wall.
after: The north side, near the ancient hills. Look for smoke at dawn.
Eight or ten. Good armour. Do not underestimate him.
A few tents and a wagon. They look harmless until they are not.
Not a fixed one. He moves every few days. Look for fresh tracks.

say: Salt is dead? The Guild is relieved. The dust road is a little safer.
A bandit ledger closed. The Guild pays.
You ended him. The Guild doesn't forget. Take the cats.
Rennik Salt is no more. Good work. Here's the coin.
A Tech Hunter in your company has a score with Slate Fennick. We have a score too. He sells stolen finds.
Fennick took a find from one of ours and sold it to a collector. The Hunter with you wants him.
The Hunters keep a list of thieves. Slate Fennick tops it. A man with you was his victim. Remove him.
Fennick is a thief and a coward. Someone travelling with you knows him.
accepted: Ask the Mercenary Guild where Fennick drinks. They hire swords like his. Then deal with him.
A guild man first. They know every sword in the north. Then Fennick.
Find a Mercenary Guild man. Ask about Fennick. Then end it.
The Guild hires; they know. Ask. Then act.

say: Fennick? He left the Guild owing us a favour and a sword. He's on the northern roads, with a small crew. Not good company.
A name we don't use. Slate Fennick hires out to whoever pays. His last job was a thief's job.
Slate Fennick. I wouldn't say his name in a Guild hall. He's near the northern flats, last I heard.
He sold relics to a collector and left a Hunter to rot. We don't approve. He's in the north.
after: A few mercenaries. Hired swords, no loyalty. Watch for them.
The northern flats, near the old road. You will find his camp by the stolen goods.
Be careful. He is good with a blade. Better with a lie.
A sword and a satchel of old things. The satchel is the prize.

say: Fennick is dead? A thief fewer. The Hunters pay. Here's your share.
A relic thief ended. We thank you. Cats.
You did the Hunters a favour. Here is the reward.
Slate Fennick is no more. Good.
A former overseer travels with you. He wants Brannoch Teel. So do we. Teel hunts our runaways on the floodwaters.
Teel is a name that makes the Swamp quiet. A man with you once worked for him and wants out.
Brannoch Teel. Slave hunter. A man with you knows his habits.
You travel with a man who served Teel. He isn't forgiven, but he's useful. Find Teel and end him.
accepted: Ask the Slave Traders. Their men talk when coin is shown. Then the floodwaters.
A trader first. They know Teel's routes. Then end him.
Find a Slave Trader who will sell the road. Then Teel.
Slavers sell each other cheaply. Ask. Then act.

say: Teel? Slave Hunter. He takes runaways on the flood road. Half the market owes him, the other half fears him. What do you want with him?
That name. I won't say it twice. Teel moves with a dozen hunters. Floodwaters, desert edge.
Brannoch Teel? He's a professional. Careful. He's past the floodwaters, hunting something.
You want Teel? For coin, I'll tell you. He passed the hard shoulder this month. He's near the desert edge.
after: A dozen, some on mounts. Do not take the road openly.
Wherever the runaways go. He tracks them to the swamp and the desert.
He is good at his job. That is the problem.
Heads and coin. In that order. I would watch his back.

say: Teel is dead? The Swamp breathes easier.
A slave hunter fewer. The Swamp thanks you.
You ended him. A runaway somewhere sleeps tonight.
Brannoch Teel is gone. Good. Here's your reward.
A medic in your company has been asking after Hob Lenner. I bought a field kit off him once and found blood in the lining. I'd be glad to see him ended.
Hob Lenner sells kits he strips from the wounded. A woman with you knows the trade. I'd pay to have him stop.
Lenner is a Reaver who robs the hurt. Someone travelling with you has bandaged his leavings. Find him, and I'll make it worth your while.
I won't deal with Hob Lenner again. If your medic wants him found, so do I. The road is poorer for him.
accepted: Ask the United Cities guard about Reaver camps on the coast. Then find Lenner.
A City guard first. They log Reaver raids. Then Lenner.
Find a UC watchman. Ask about Lenner. Then proceed.
The coast is Reaver ground. A guard will know. Then deal with him.

say: Hob Lenner? Reaver. He hunts the old beach and the pits. Careful. He has friends.
Lenner sells armour and kills wounded men for it. He works the red coast. Don't go in the open.
A Reaver with a knife and no scruples. He's near the old pits. That's all I'll say.
Lenner is a monster. I'm glad someone wants him. He's near the coast.
after: The old beach, east end. Look for skinned rocks. That is his marker.
A few whelps. Young, hungry, fast. Do not underestimate them.
Be careful. The coast is wet and the sand is soft.
A long knife and a bag of stolen kits. You will know him by the smell.

say: Lenner is dead? Then the kits on my shelf are the last he sold.
A robber of the wounded gone. I will sleep better. Cats.
You ended Hob Lenner. A patient somewhere will heal in peace.
I keep my word. Lenner is gone.
A worker in your company has asked about Dolan Pike. We know him. He leads hungry men. He burned a hive.
Dolan Pike took a hive's stores and left it to burn. A worker with you was there. We would like him stopped.
Pike is a name we avoid. A worker among your company carries the grief. We feel it. End it.
Dolan Pike. Starving. Violent. A worker with you wants him stopped. So do we.
accepted: Ask a City guard about the hungry bandits. They keep a record. Then find Pike in the dry edge.
A guard first. They know the bandits' marches. Then Pike.
Find a UC watchman. Ask about Pike. Then act.
The bandits move with the hunger. A guard knows where. Then go.

say: Pike? Hungry bandit chief. His men chase caravans and hives. He's near the dry edge. Don't give him bread.
Dolan Pike is thin and mean. His mob is thinner. They're in the desert, between towns.
A bandit who ate his own boots. He leads a mob. They don't stop. Dry edge, last I heard.
He isn't hard to find. Follow the empty barrels. He's in the dry edge.
after: A dozen. All hungry. All desperate. Do not underestimate them.
East of here, near the ruins. They camp in dry riverbeds.
Be careful. Starving men fight harder than fed men.
Food. He wants food. He will take what he can.

say: Pike is dead? The hungry will be quieter.
A bandit leader fewer. The hive thanks you. Cats.
You ended Dolan Pike. The worker will sleep better.
Pike is gone. Good. Here's your reward.
One of our own travels with you. She has been asking about Isolde Marr. We know the name. She sold a cell and stayed free. Remove her.
Marr is a name the village doesn't forget. A sister with you has the right to ask. We pay for her answer.
Isolde Marr sold twenty of ours. A woman with you knows the number. End her.
The Flotsam Ninjas are patient. Marr isn't safe forever. Someone with you is the reason.
accepted: Ask the free traders where mercenaries drink. They sell to everyone. Then find Marr.
A Free Trader first. They see every sword for hire. Then Marr.
Find a trader. Ask about Marr. Then act.
Traders gossip. Ask them. Then find her.

say: Isolde Marr? Mercenary captain. She drinks where the pay is good and the questions are few. She works the northern flats.
That name. I sold her bandages once. She pays well and tips poorly. Last seen north of here.
Marr? She leads a small band. Quiet, deadly. She's near the old forest edge.
A mercenary with a past. I wouldn't cross her. But I don't like what she did.
after: A handful. Good steel. Careful.
The northern flats, near the forest. Look for a red banner.
Be careful. She is clever. Do not underestimate her.
She sleeps lightly. Do not give her a reason to wake.

say: Marr is dead? The village will sleep better. Here's the payment.
A traitor ended. The Flotsam Ninjas thank you.
You did what we could not. Here is the reward.
Isolde Marr is no more. A debt paid.
Sit if you like. I sit facing the door.
You have the look of someone who pays. Is that so?
Can I help you? That's a real question, I rarely ask it.
Hands where I can see them. Habit.
Who are you?
You have a face I'd remember. Who are you?
And you are?
Who are you, stranger?
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: Venna. I was owned eleven years. Now I'm owned by nobody, which is lonelier than it sounds.
A Greenlander who ran. The shackles left their marks and I wear long sleeves in the heat.
Somebody's ex-property. Ask the Swamp, half the faces here are the same.
Would you come with us?
Join my squad. Name a price.
What do you charge?
Would you travel with us?
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: 1200 cats. Not for the work. For the bed I paid for and the debts I wouldn't leave behind.
1200. I stay with you till I'm paid in a way that isn't coin.
My price is 1200. Take it or find a sword that cares less.
Here. That should do it.
Agreed. Here's the coin.
Count it if you like.
Here's your fee.
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: Done. If you ever put a chain on me, I'll use it on you.
Right. I carry my own bundle.
Then I'm yours, not owned.
I can't afford that right now.
I don't have that much on me.
That's more than I carry.
Let me find the money first.
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: Then come back when you have it. I'm not going anywhere.
A shame. I'd have liked the road.
Cats first. I've been talked into worse for less.
Never mind. I have changed my mind.
I'll think about it.
No, I don't think so.
That isn't what I wanted to hear.
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: No harm. Watch your back out there.
Right. The door is behind you.
Then go. Don't let the door catch you.
That's all I wanted to know.
Good to know. Goodbye.
I'll be going.
Thanks. I'll be on my way.
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: Why are you still here?
Why do you sit here alone?
You don't look like you belong here. Why stay?
Why are you not out on the road?
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: Because the Swamp is where the runaways end up, and the slavers know it. Staying put feels like waiting for them.
Every month somebody new walks in here with a collar scar. One day it will be somebody I know.
A bar is a poor place to hide but a good place to watch the door. I am tired of watching.
Would you come with us?
Join my squad. Name a price.
What do you charge?
Would you travel with us?
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: 1200 cats. Not for the work. For the bed I paid for and the debts I wouldn't leave behind.
1200. I stay with you till I'm paid in a way that isn't coin.
My price is 1200. Take it or find a sword that cares less.
Here. That should do it.
Agreed. Here's the coin.
Count it if you like.
Here's your fee.
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: Done. If you ever put a chain on me, I'll use it on you.
Right. I carry my own bundle.
Then I'm yours, not owned.
I can't afford that right now.
